findings.where: Hero, the line beside the name and the CTA ('Advice on infrastructure projects… from a former Lead Lawyer in the World Bank's PPP Group, with over 40 years…'), and the role block under the name
findings.fault: The first screen speaks about Mark in the third person, in a CV voice, and leans on a size claim ('over 40 years'). The only picture is a drawing, so Mark is neither seen nor heard in his own words. The brief makes him the brand, but this first screen reads like a firm describing its lead.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brief says 'the man himself, seen and heard, in his own words' and 'the individual is the brand', not a firm's voice. A development-bank officer coming from LinkedIn, who wants to know whether a real, named person speaks to them and what they did, not adjectives of size.

findings.where: Hero, the role block under the name ('INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS'), the circled 'A' marker, the title-block cells 'DRAWING MMM-GA-001' and 'SCALE NTS', and 'NTS', 'EQ' and '±0.00' on the drawing
findings.fault: Drawing-office jargon sits in the visitor's reading path and is never explained. 'NTS', 'Section A-A' and a drawing number are set in the same block and type as Mark's role, so the identity line reads as a mix of who he is and meaningless codes. On a phone the bullet is also stranded at a line end.
findings.who_objects: A procurement officer at a development bank, who is a lawyer or economist, not a draughtsman. They meet unexplained codes in the line that should say who Mark is (first-visit trust item 11: technical terms explained once).

findings.where: Nav bar / title block, the 'DRAWING MMM-GA-001' and 'SCALE NTS' cells (desktop: right end of the bar; phone: beside the logo, above the links)
findings.fault: Two static cells are drawn in the same ruled boxes, in the same spaced capitals and colour, as the four nav links beside them. Nothing tells a visitor which cells go somewhere. On a phone they take the top row, the place where links are expected.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning the bar for where to go, who taps 'MMM-GA-001' and gets nothing (a false affordance from similarity with the nav).

findings.where: Nav logo and the hero drawing (the mark at full width, in white, with the third bay hatched amber); the palette tile
findings.fault: The mark appears only reversed in white linework, a version Mark does not hold, and its blue wordmark and grey arches (#0070C0, #404040) have no place in the palette, which neither gives them a job nor declares them logo-only. The diazo ground also cannot take the full-colour logo, so the whole direction depends on a recolour that needs the client's yes.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo is fixed ('the logo stays') and whose blue wordmark disappears from his own site. Angélique, who will reuse the logo with no rule for which version goes on which ground.

findings.where: Hero drawing, the sodium-amber hatch in the third bay, against the amber 'WRITE TO MARK' button
findings.fault: The action's colour is also used as decoration. The amber hatch is the loudest mark in the drawing and sits above and before the button, so the eye lands on decoration first and the one action loses its claim on that colour.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to get in touch: the colour that should mean 'act here' also means 'a picture', which weakens the only call to action (primary-action colour reserved for A).

findings.where: First screen and the page as a whole (no footer)
findings.fault: There is no proof that Mark has done this kind of work: no named body that asked for his work, no publication or talk near the action, no regions of work and no audience named ('for whom', 'where'). The email address is never shown as text, and there is no footer with contact details or a current date. Real items exist (the World Bank role, the dated lecture) but are not placed as proof.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has to justify contacting an individual consultant and wants to see work for bodies like theirs, in their region, before writing (first-visit trust items 2, 3, 6, 7, 13, 14). No proof should be invented to fill this.

findings.where: Article specimen ('The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'), body text and pull quote set over the blueprint grid
findings.fault: Long-form reading text sits light-on-blue directly over the visible grid, whose lines run through the paragraphs. The page meant for reading keeps the full texture of the display surface, which makes the reading surface busy.
findings.who_objects: A reader working through one of Mark's articles of several hundred words, who has to read through a ruled pattern. Mark, who finds busy pages off-putting.

findings.where: The direction as a system: the title block's drawing number and scale, section letters, dimension annotations
findings.fault: The look depends on drawing metadata that each new page needs: a drawing number, a section letter, a scale. A lay editor adding a post or a PDF either has to make these up or leaves them stale and meaningless.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who must be able to add an article without inventing engineering codes (client value 9). Mark, if every page carries the same 'MMM-GA-001'.

findings.where: Type pair tile against the article specimen heading; the 'REPLAY THE CUT' button against the article's underlined link
findings.fault: Like parts are not treated alike. The tile states that headings are ExtraBold tracked capitals, but the article heading is set in sentence case. The 'Replay the cut' button is drawn as underlined text, the same treatment as the article's link, so a button and a link share one look.
findings.who_objects: The layout round's designer and Angélique, who inherit two contradictory heading rules and a button that looks like a link.

findings.where: Phone, the texture tile (earth hatch and poche) and the motion timeline table
findings.fault: At phone width the hatch swatch sits flush against the frame's left edge and the poche against its right, and the dimension line is gone, leaving an empty ruled strip. The timeline table squeezes element names onto three lines, and its easing column says only 'plot'.
findings.who_objects: The founder or Mark reviewing the tile on a phone, who sees a broken specimen rather than the texture as it would appear.

findings.where: Hero drawing, the loose curve rising off the right end of the ground line; desktop third slice, the empty area left of the motion card
findings.fault: The unexplained S-curve at the right edge reads as a stray or unfinished line on an otherwise exact drawing. Below the article, the left column ends early and leaves a large empty block beside the tall motion card.
findings.who_objects: A careful visitor who reads the sheet as 'measured, exact', and is jarred by a line that belongs to nothing and by the lopsided bottom of the page.
